name: Ephedrine

lead: Ephedrine is a stimulant from Ephedra plants, used medically to raise blood pressure during anesthesia. In looksmaxxing it is known as the ephedrine, caffeine and aspirin (ECA) stack, used for appetite suppression and energy during fasted cardio while cutting toward a leaner physique.

It stimulates adrenergic receptors and triggers norepinephrine release, which raises heart rate, blood pressure, alertness and energy expenditure and suppresses appetite. A 2003 JAMA meta-analysis examined it for weight loss and athletic performance, and a general reference summarises the findings as modest short-term weight loss, about 0.9 kg per month more than placebo. It is a milder thermogenic than clenbuterol or DNP.

paras: Guides on looksmax.org describe it as increasing energy and reducing hunger during a cut, typically as the ECA stack, with heart-health cautions attached. Forum users also pair it with MK-677 to offset hunger.

Reported effects include palpitations, fast heart rate, high blood pressure, restlessness and nausea, with more heart-related events than placebo in the meta-analysis. The FDA banned ephedrine-alkaloid dietary supplements in 2004; the injectable is prescription-only.

angle.text: Ephedrine is the stimulant in the classic ECA stack, used to suppress appetite and lift energy for fasted cardio while cutting toward a leaner physique. It works by stimulating adrenergic receptors and releasing norepinephrine. Trials show modest fat loss, with raised heart rate and blood pressure.

lead: Ephedrine is a sympathomimetic amine and central nervous system stimulant found naturally in plants of the genus Ephedra (ma huang) and also made synthetically [1]. It acts on adrenergic receptors and triggers release of norepinephrine, producing raised blood pressure, heart rate and alertness [1][2]. In current US medical practice it is a prescription injectable indicated for clinically important hypotension during anesthesia [2].

In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities ephedrine is discussed as a fat-loss and appetite-suppression aid, most often as the "ECA stack" of ephedrine, caffeine and aspirin [3][4]. Guides on looksmax.org describe it as increasing energy and reducing hunger during a cut, and typically attach heart-health cautions [3][4].

A 2003 JAMA meta-analysis examined ephedra and ephedrine for weight loss and athletic performance [5]. A general reference summarises the clinical evidence as showing modest short-term weight loss of about 0.9 kg per month more than placebo, alongside increased heart rate and cardiovascular risk; the US FDA banned ephedrine-alkaloid dietary supplements in 2004 [1].

paras: The current US label for ephedrine sulfate injection lists treatment of clinically important hypotension in the setting of anesthesia as its indication [2]. Many registered trials compare ephedrine with norepinephrine or phenylephrine for blood-pressure control during spinal anesthesia for caesarean delivery [6][7]. Historically it has also been used as a bronchodilator for asthma, a nasal decongestant, and for urinary incontinence [1].
Ephedrine is used by people seeking leaner physiques as a thermogenic and appetite suppressant, usually combined with caffeine, as in the ECA stack [3][4]. This use is not an approved indication.

A 2003 meta-analysis in JAMA reviewed controlled trials of ephedra and ephedrine for weight loss and athletic performance [5]. A general reference summarising this literature reports about 0.9 kg per month greater weight loss than placebo for ephedrine-containing products over the short term [1]. A caffeine review notes that caffeine itself is an ergogenic aid that allows longer or more intense training, which is part of the rationale given for stacking [8].

A study in ten healthy volunteers found that ephedrine increased blood pressure, heart rate and energy expenditure, and raised circulating glucose, insulin and thyroid hormones, but did not activate brown adipose tissue the way cold exposure did [9].

The injectable label lists nausea, vomiting, tachycardia, palpitations, reactive hypertension, bradycardia, dizziness and restlessness among reported reactions, and warns about tachyphylaxis with repeated dosing and about severe hypertension when combined with oxytocic drugs [2]. A general reference states that increased heart rate and cardiovascular events risk prompted the FDA to declare ephedrine-alkaloid supplements adulterated in 2004 [1].

A looksmax.org guide author says the stack raises resting heart rate by at least 10 beats per minute and warns against high-intensity interval training while on it; another guide says not to use it with heart problems [3][4].

Ephedrine directly stimulates alpha- and beta-adrenergic receptors and indirectly causes release of norepinephrine from sympathetic nerve terminals; the label ascribes its pressor effect to increased arterial pressure, cardiac output and peripheral resistance [2]. Amphetamine-type stimulants release norepinephrine more potently than dopamine or serotonin [10]. Comparative studies in humans from 1971 measured its effects against amphetamine, methamphetamine and methylphenidate [11].

Ephedrine is a phenethylamine; the natural form is the (1R,2S) enantiomer, and pseudoephedrine is its diastereomer [1]. It occurs in more than 40 Ephedra species, though industrial production relies mainly on semi-synthetic routes [1]. Nagayoshi Nagai first isolated it in 1885, and Keishi Chen and Carl Schmidt revived it for asthma in the 1920s [1].

In the United States, the FDA declared dietary supplements containing ephedrine alkaloids adulterated and banned their sale in 2004 [1]. The injectable form is a prescription drug [2]. A looksmax.org guide notes that availability depends on national law and describes the oral form as the hardest component of the stack to source [3].

On looksmax.org the ECA stack is promoted for appetite suppression, energy for cardio and mild thermogenesis, often described as weaker than clenbuterol or DNP [3][4]. A 17-year-old poster asked about combining it with the growth hormone secretagogue MK-677, and a reply raised the question of whether a calorie deficit would hinder growth [12]. On T Nation, members mention ECA among fat-loss options, including in combination with other cutting agents and DNP [13][14][15].

A 2003 JAMA meta-analysis pooled randomised trials of ephedra and ephedrine for weight loss and athletic performance [5]. A randomised trial in myasthenia gravis and a clinical trial on hemostatic effects have also been published, but they address different conditions [16][17]. In anesthesia, numerous trials compare ephedrine with other vasopressors; several are registered for caesarean delivery [6][7]. A mechanistic study found it raises energy expenditure in healthy volunteers [9].

lore.intro: Ephedrine appears on looksmax.org mainly through the ECA stack, presented as an appetite-suppressing, energising aid for cutting, with frequent heart-safety disclaimers [3][4].

claims.claim: The ECA stack kills appetite and gives energy for fasted cardio while preserving lean tissue.
ECA is a mild thermogenic, much weaker than clenbuterol, albuterol or DNP.
It is acceptable if you have no heart problems and track heart rate, and exercise should be low-intensity.
Ephedrine can be stacked with MK-677 to counter hunger while building muscle and height.

timeline.event: Nagayoshi Nagai first isolates ephedrine from Ephedra [1].
Chen and Schmidt promote ephedrine for asthma in Western medicine [1].
JAMA meta-analysis of ephedra and ephedrine for weight loss and performance [5].
FDA bans dietary supplements containing ephedrine alkaloids [1].
